response.title: How many solar panels do I need to fully recharge a large home backup power station in one sunny day?
response.answer:
For a large home backup power station, you'll typically need 4–12 solar panels rated at 400W each to fully recharge it in one sunny day, depending on the battery capacity.

Assuming about 5 peak sun hours per day and 80% overall charging efficiency, here's what you can expect.

Idealized daily energy estimate. Your power station must support the total solar input voltage, current and wattage; otherwise adding panels may not increase charging speed.
Three important considerations

Solar input limit: A power station with a maximum 1,000W solar input cannot use the full output of a 3,000W array.

Location and season: In sunny California, 5 peak sun hours can be a reasonable planning assumption, but winter, clouds and shading can significantly reduce output.

Panel orientation: Properly tilted, unshaded panels generally outperform panels laid flat or placed behind windows.

markup:
For a large home backup power station, you'll typically need **4–12 solar panels rated at 400W each** to fully recharge it in one sunny day, depending on the battery capacity.

Assuming about **5 peak sun hours per day** and 80% overall charging efficiency, here's what you can expect.

## Solar panels needed by battery size

| Battery capacity | 400W panels needed | Total solar capacity |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2 kWh | 2 | 800 W |
| 4 kWh | 3 | 1,200 W |
| 6 kWh | 4 | 1,600 W |
| 10 kWh | 7 | 2,800 W |
| 15 kWh | 10 | 4,000 W |
| 20 kWh | 13 | 5,200 W |

These estimates assume charging from 0% to 100%, with no simultaneous household power consumption.

## Calculate your own setup

{@body const [capacity,setCapacity] = DIL.useState(10)}
{@body const [panel,setPanel] = DIL.useState("400")}
{@body const [sun,setSun] = DIL.useState(5)}
{@body const [eff,setEff] = DIL.useState(80)}
{@body const panels = Math.ceil(capacity*1000/(Number(panel)*sun*eff/100))}
<box border radius="2xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <text weight="medium">Solar charging calculator</text>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    <text size="sm">Battery capacity</text>
    <title size="lg" color="default" tabularNums>{capacity} kWh</title>
  </row>
  <slider min={2} max={30} step={1} value={capacity} onChange={setCapacity}/>
  <label>Solar panel wattage</label>
  <radio-group value={panel} onChange={setPanel} direction="row">
    <radio value="200">200W</radio>
    <radio value="400">400W</radio>
    <radio value="500">500W</radio>
  </radio-group>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    <text size="sm">Peak sun hours</text>
    **{sun} hours**
  </row>
  <slider min={3} max={7} step={0.5} value={sun} onChange={setSun}/>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    <text size="sm">Charging efficiency</text>
    **{eff}%**
  </row>
  <slider min={65} max={90} step={5} value={eff} onChange={setEff}/>
  <box background="surface-secondary" radius="xl" padding={3} gap={2}>
    <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">ESTIMATED PANELS REQUIRED</text>
    <row align="baseline" gap={2}>
      <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{panels}</title>
      <text>× {panel}W panels</text>
    </row>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <row justify="between">
      <text color="secondary" size="sm">Total rated solar power</text>
      **{(panels*Number(panel)/1000).toFixed(1)} kW**
    </row>
    <row justify="between">
      <text color="secondary" size="sm">Estimated daily energy</text>
      **{(panels*Number(panel)*sun*eff/100/1000).toFixed(1)} kWh**
    </row>
  </box>
  <caption>Idealized daily energy estimate. Your power station must support the total solar input voltage, current and wattage; otherwise adding panels may not increase charging speed.</caption>
</box>

## Three important considerations

1. **Solar input limit:** A power station with a maximum 1,000W solar input cannot use the full output of a 3,000W array.
2. **Location and season:** In sunny California, 5 peak sun hours can be a reasonable planning assumption, but winter, clouds and shading can significantly reduce output.
3. **Panel orientation:** Properly tilted, unshaded panels generally outperform panels laid flat or placed behind windows.

## What power station do you have?

For example, is it an <Entity category="product" value="EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3"/>, <Entity category="product" value="Anker SOLIX F3800"/>, <Entity category="product" value="Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus"/>, or another model?

**Tell me the brand and model (or its battery capacity in kWh)**, and I can calculate the panel count, recommended configuration, and whether its solar charging input can actually support a full recharge in one day.
